questions.q:
Pertaining to manuscript heritage, consider the following pairs:
Manuscript or project : Associated with
1. Bakhshali Manuscript : Early discussion of zero
2. Rigveda Samhita : UNESCO recognition
3. Timbuktu Manuscripts Project : Egypt
4. Kautilya's Arthashastra manuscript : Preservation at Taxila
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Bakhshali is known in the history of mathematics. Rigveda manuscripts entered UNESCO's Memory of the World Register, which shows soft power potential. Pair 4 is wrong, as the Arthashastra manuscript that revived knowledge of ancient statecraft is preserved at Mysore. Pair 3 is wrong as well because Timbuktu is in Mali, and the project is cited as a model of public participation, having trained local conservators and revived traditional bookbinding. Preserving heritage also connects with the Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(f).

questions.q:
With reference to the second Mahad conference of December 1927, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The planned satyagraha was postponed by Ambedkar after a temporary injunction was obtained in a suit claiming that the tank was private property.
2. The Manusmriti was publicly burnt at Mahad on 25 December 1927.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Both are correct. Facing the injunction, Ambedkar chose not to march to the tank, showing respect for legal process while the suit went on, and the High Court decided the matter in 1937. The same gathering burnt the Manusmriti, a symbolic rejection of the text seen as justifying caste hierarchy. The date is still marked by many as Manusmriti Dahan Divas. The episode shows that the movement challenged both civil exclusion and the ideology underlying it.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 83-84; Manusmriti burning is static

questions.q:
Statement-I: Article 15 of the Constitution bars denial of access to public wells and tanks on grounds including caste.
Statement-II: Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but the second does not explain the first. Article 15(2) is a distinct non-discrimination guarantee which names wells and tanks among public places, while Article 17 separately ends untouchability and makes its practice punishable. Each stands on its own. The Mahad Satyagraha of 1927 is commonly linked to both, because the fight to draw water from a public tank challenged exclusion and also the idea of pollution by touch. Its centenary year therefore invites this constitutional reading.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 83-84; Article 15(2) text is static

questions.q:
In respect of the Gyan Bharatam Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It is a central sector scheme under the Ministry of Culture.
2. It builds on the National Mission for Manuscripts.
3. It proposes using OCR, AI and blockchain for access, transcription and provenance.
4. The national survey under it will generate a 'Manuscript Presence Map'.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. Being a central sector scheme, the Mission has no Centre-State cost sharing. It extends the earlier national mission, with the goal of digitising over one crore manuscripts and creating a national digital repository. The survey's geo-tagged inventory supports cataloguing and conservation planning. Technology is needed because scripts are complex and many documents are hard to read, and trained palaeographers are few.

questions.q:
Regarding anti-caste organisations of the pre-independence era, consider the following pairs:
Organisation or movement : Associated figure
1. Satyashodhak Samaj : Jyotirao Phule
2. Harijan Sevak Sangh : Mahatma Gandhi
3. Self-Respect Movement : Sree Narayana Guru
4. Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha : B.R. Ambedkar
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to free lower castes from religious exploitation, Gandhi set up the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932, and Ambedkar's Sabha of 1924 organised the Mahad protest. Pair 3 is wrong: the Self-Respect Movement of 1925 was founded by E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar) in Tamil Nadu, while Sree Narayana Guru led a separate reform movement in Kerala. These bodies ranged from radical rejection of hierarchy to reform from within.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 83-84; Sree Narayana Guru is static

questions.q:
Consider the following languages:
1. English
2. Rajasthani
3. Santali
4. Konkani
5. Bhojpuri
How many of the above are among the languages recognised for the Sahitya Akademi Awards?
questions.e: The first four are recognised and Bhojpuri is not. The Akademi's 24 languages comprise the 22 in the Eighth Schedule, which include Santali and Konkani, plus English and Rajasthani, which are not in the Schedule but were added by the Akademi itself. Bhojpuri is neither in the Eighth Schedule nor on the Akademi's list, despite a long-standing demand. The trap is to assume that the award list mirrors the Schedule exactly; it goes beyond it in two cases.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 86; Eighth Schedule membership is static

questions.q: The Bhasha Samman, one of the honours given by the Sahitya Akademi, recognises
o: the best translation of a foreign classic into English
contributions to languages outside the Akademi's recognised list and to classical and medieval literature
the best children's book in each recognised language
writers below 35 years of age writing in the Eighth Schedule languages
questions.e: The Bhasha Samman honours work in languages that the Akademi does not formally recognise, along with classical and medieval literature, and so extends its reach beyond the 24 languages. The other descriptions fit different prizes: translations are honoured by the Translation Prize, though among Indian languages rather than foreign classics; younger writers by the Yuva Puraskar; and children's writing by the Bal Sahitya Puraskar. The main annual award, a plaque with Rs 1 lakh, goes to outstanding books in the recognised languages.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 86; Bhasha Samman purpose is static

questions.q:
Arrange the following events linked to the Mahad struggle in chronological order:
1. Bombay High Court ruling that the Chawdar Tank was public property
2. Bombay Legislative Council resolution on access to public watering places
3. Founding of the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
4. Ambedkar's procession to the tank during the Kolaba District Depressed Classes Conference
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Council resolution came in 1923 and was followed in 1924 by the founding of the Sabha, which later organised the protest. The conference and procession took place on 19-20 March 1927. Legal finality came only on 17 March 1937, when the High Court held the tank to be open to all. The order brings out the central point: formal rights existed on paper for years, and it took direct action and long litigation to make them real.

questions.q:
With reference to the Sahitya Akademi, consider the following statements:
1. It was created by an Act of Parliament as a statutory body.
2. It functions under the Union Ministry of Education.
3. It is registered as a society.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. The Akademi began as a government initiative under Maulana Azad, was formally set up in 1952, inaugurated on 12 March 1954 and registered as a society in 1956, so statement 1 is wrong: government initiation does not mean creation by statute. Statement 2 is wrong because it is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture. As the National Academy of Letters it gives awards in 24 languages, first conferred in 1955, along with prizes such as the Yuva Puraskar.

questions.q:
With reference to the impact of the Mahad Satyagraha, consider the following statements:
1. Jamnalal Bajaj opened the Lakshminarayan Temple at Wardha to Dalits in 1928.
2. Ambedkar compared Mahad with the French National Assembly of 1789.
3. It helped pave the way for the Kalaram Temple entry movement at Nashik in 1930.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The protest pushed the national movement to confront untouchability, which is reflected in Bajaj's temple opening and in the Congress reconstituting its anti-untouchability sub-committee under Madan Mohan Malaviya. Ambedkar's comparison presented the assembly as a founding moment for liberty, equality and fraternity. The Nashik agitation extended the fight from access to water to entry into temples. The participation of Dalit women on an unprecedented scale was another consequence worth keeping in mind.
